candidates.name: alfred (R package, CRAN)
candidates.what_it_holds: R client for ALFRED (Archival FRED) that pulls historical data releases / vintages for any FRED series with no API key required; returns tidy data frames of a series as it was known at any given past date. Example series shown: INDPRO. On CRAN since June 2017, last functional update 26 Jul 2021; mirrored at github.com/cran/alfred (0 stars, but that's just the CRAN read-only mirror).
candidates.why_useful: Directly implements gap #4 (ALFRED-style macro vintages). Gives point-in-time snapshots of any FRED series (GDP, PCE, CPI, payrolls, industrial production) as they stood on a given historical date -- exactly what's needed to refit at guide dates per the repo's point-in-time rule rather than using today's revised macro series as an input to nowcasts of consumer spend/travel demand.
candidates.time_coverage: Whatever vintage history FRED/ALFRED expose per series (many series back to 1990s-2000s vintages)
candidates.size_hint: small R package, no committed data (live API pulls)

candidates.name: fredapi
candidates.what_it_holds: Python wrapper (1,657 stars, updated as recently as 13 Sep 2026) around the FRED API with explicit ALFRED vintage support: get_series_first_release(), get_series_latest_release(), get_series_as_of_date(), get_series_all_releases(), get_series_vintage_dates(). Returns pandas Series/DataFrames; tracks realtime_start/realtime_end per observation.
candidates.why_useful: The most mature, actively-maintained Python tool for exactly the point-in-time macro discipline the repo's rules require (rule 2: refit at guide dates, vendor+timestamp per value). Could backstop or replace ad hoc FRED pulls currently in data/processed with proper vintage-as-of-date retrieval for any macro series used as a nowcast input (CPI lodging, PCE travel, etc.).
candidates.time_coverage: Full FRED/ALFRED vintage history per series

candidates.name: FredFetch
candidates.what_it_holds: MATLAB package with fred.latest(series) and fred.vint(series, vintage_date) for pulling FRED/ALFRED data at a specific vintage date, including a 'pseudo-vintage' mode that simulates publication lag for series without full ALFRED vintage history, plus parallelized bulk downloads across many series/vintage dates.
candidates.why_useful: Same ALFRED vintage capability as fredapi but for MATLAB users, and notably adds simulated publication-delay handling for series that lack full vintage archives -- useful if the team needs point-in-time treatment of a FRED series ALFRED doesn't fully vintage.

candidates.name: fred-mcp
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP (Model Context Protocol) server exposing FRED's 800k+ series plus ALFRED vintage data ('the numbers before revisions') as a tool interface, updated 20 Aug 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Lower priority than fredapi/alfred but notable as a very recent (Aug 2026), actively maintained wrapper if the team wants ALFRED access exposed as an agent tool rather than a library call.

candidates.name: macro-dashboard (zero-cost US macro forecasting engine)
candidates.what_it_holds: Vintage-true backtesting harness pulling 84 FRED series + full ALFRED vintages (~3,800 API calls for a full backtest) + BLS CPI/employment + Yahoo Finance gold, with release-date filtering, real ALFRED vintages, and expanding (not full-sample) z-scores to close look-ahead leak channels; validated over 147 quarterly as-of dates since 1990, 695 scored points, 0 leaks. No data files are committed -- everything is pulled live via tools/backfill.py.
candidates.why_useful: This is close to a working template for exactly the 'vintage-aware backtest' methodology gap #17/#4 calls for -- release-date filtering + real vintages + expanding-window normalization is the standard fix for the leakage problems the repo's own backtests must avoid. Worth reading as a reference implementation, not as a data source (no committed data).

candidates.name: macro-treasury-futures (point-in-time macro ML strategy)
candidates.what_it_holds: Point-in-time macro ML strategy for Treasury futures using ALFRED vintage data (CPI, payrolls, unemployment, industrial production, jobless claims -> 24 features) with leakage-safe, expanding-window Ridge regression; backtested 2020-Jul 2026 (3.85% annual return, 0.50 Sharpe, 52% hit rate). No Airbnb relevance directly but a second worked example of ALFRED-vintage + leakage-safe backtest design.
candidates.why_useful: Secondary reference implementation for vintage-aware, leakage-safe backtest design (same rationale as macro-dashboard above); the feature-engineering pattern (release-date-aligned macro surprises) could be adapted to the ABNB consumer-strength regional split workstream.

candidates.name: cran/alfred (read-only CRAN mirror)
candidates.what_it_holds: Automated read-only mirror of the CRAN 'alfred' package (same package as onnokleen/alfred above), synced 2023-03-21.
candidates.why_useful: Duplicate pointer to onnokleen/alfred; flagged only so it isn't mistaken for a separate tool. No new content.

notes: gh search repos was very sensitive to phrasing: multi-word quoted queries against 'Philadelphia Fed real-time dataset', 'vintage macro data', 'real-time data revisions', and 'real-time database macroeconomists' all returned zero rows (the search API appears to require terms that actually co-occur in repo name/description text, not a natural-language description), while short keyword combos ('alfred fred vintages', 'ALFRED', 'alfred R vintages', 'vintage backtest macro') worked. A bare 'ALFRED' query mostly returned the Alfred macOS/Windows launcher ecosystem (Wox, Flow.Launcher, alfred-workflow, etc.) -- all irrelevant and excluded. No hits at all for the Philadelphia Fed's own 'Real-Time Data Research Center' / SPF vintage dataset by name, for ONS (UK) revision-tracking tooling, or for Eurostat-specific vintage/revision packages (tried 'eurostat vintage revisions'); the underlying academic Philly Fed real-time dataset and ONS revisions triangle are evidently not mirrored or wrapped as popular/discoverable GitHub repos, or my query terms didn't match how such repos would self-describe. WebSearch quota for this whole multi-agent run was already exhausted (0 of budget left) before I could fall back to site:github.com queries for those two gaps, so Philly Fed RTDSM tooling and ONS/Eurostat vintage packages remain unconfirmed by this scout -- a follow-up scout with fresh WebSearch budget should specifically try 'RTDSM' and 'real-time data set macroeconomists' and 'ONS revisions triangle' as gh search terms (short, not natural-language) and via WebSearch site:github.com. Everything found is US-FRED/ALFRED-centric tooling (acquisition_method, not stored datasets) -- none carry committed historical vintage data files, so all fill gap #4 as *methods* the team could run against FRED/ALFRED live, not as new stored data. No repo here mentions Airbnb; all are general macro/quant infrastructure, in scope per CONTEXT.md's point-in-time vintage priority.
